## Meaning

The LX repo preserves the Liris one-direction chain sentence and token-saving address-language surface. The IX repo preserves the Acer original index-language surface: IX numbers as vocabulary, chains as sentences, and catalogs as dictionaries. Together they form a public two-seat bridge:

`	ext
LIRIS LX chain sentence -> ACER IX index-language target -> tools/skills/program slots -> later BEHCS/HBI/HBP receipt ladder
`

This bridge packet exists so neither repo can be read as an isolated note. The public claim is narrower and stronger: the two repos are reciprocal public anchors for the same original index-language/token-savings lineage.

## Boundary

This bridge does not assert that every private local byte is public. It asserts that the public receipt families now mutually identify each other and preserve the LX/IX layer boundary.
